note: Work: the Children's Protection and Welfare Act, 2011 (Act 7 of 2011), section 228, sets the minimum age for admission of a child to employment at fifteen and forbids employing a child below it; section 229 lets a child of thirteen or above do light work. The Labour Act, 2024 (Act 3 of 2024, Gazette No. 22 of 2 April 2024), which replaced the Labour Code Order, 1992, lets a child or young person be employed in a private undertaking only if over fifteen (section 195). Both were read only in LesothoLII's own search results (the excerpts its search returns, saved as served): the acts' full pages sit behind a Cloudflare challenge, not passed, so the sections were not read whole. No exception for performers was found in the excerpts, and the 1992 Code (read whole in the text WIPO Lex holds) had none, so a performer under 15 is held as barred (a reading, not the law's word); hours limits aren't held. Majority: not read; the 2011 Act defines a child as under 18 for its own purposes, but no statute setting the age of majority was reached. Service: not read; no Lesotho defence law was reached.
